fivenumMeta: Five-Number Summaries in Meta-Analysis, Imputed Means and SDs with Standard Errors

Source: R/fivenumMeta-package.R
fivenumMeta-package.Rd

Meta-analyses often pool studies that report a median with quartiles or extremes rather than a mean and a standard deviation, and the established estimators impute the mean and the SD from those summaries. An imputed mean is not a sample mean, and its standard deviation is not \(\sigma/\sqrt{n}\). This package computes, under normality, the standard deviation factors \(C_\mu(n)\) and \(C_\sigma(n)\) such that \(SD(\hat\mu) = C_\mu(n)\,\sigma\) and \(SD(\hat\sigma) = C_\sigma(n)\,\sigma\), and the inflation factors \(\kappa_\mu(n) = C_\mu(n)\sqrt{n}\) and \(\kappa_\sigma(n) = C_\sigma(n)/\sqrt{1 - b_S(n)^2}\), exactly, from the means and covariances of the normal order statistics that the package osmoments computes, at every sample size. The estimators covered are the best linear unbiased estimator (BLUE) of the reported values, the default, and the estimators of Wan, Luo and Shi, under the data-reporting scenarios "S1" (minimum, median, maximum), "S2" (the three quartiles), "S3" (all five), and, for the BLUE, "S4" and "S5", which add the 10th and 90th percentiles to "S2" and "S3".

Details

For a meta-analysis data set, one row per study, se_imputed_df reads the scenario off the columns each row has and appends the imputed mean and SD with their naive and exact plug-in standard errors, and se_imputed_diff does the same for two groups per row and adds the effect of the study, the difference of means or the log variability ratio, with its naive and its exact standard error, in the names that metafor::rma() takes as they are. pool_imputed pools those studies in one call, under the naive and the exact standard errors side by side, by the common-effect or the DerSimonian-Laird model. For one study, se_imputed returns the same quantities from the reported values and the sample size. The factors themselves are c_mu, c_sigma and inflation_factors, with the closed-form shortcut formulas c_mu_shortcut and c_sigma_shortcut for use without the integration. The weights and the reported ranks are estimator_weights and scenario_ranks, and imputed_moments gives the variances and the covariance of the two imputed statistics. Every function defaults to the BLUE; the estimators of Wan, Luo and Shi are reached by version = "wan_luo_shi" in the study-level functions and in inflation_factors(), and by the argument method in the others.

References

Wu Z, Shi J, Tong T (2026). Precision of the imputed mean and standard deviation from a five-number summary. Manuscript. The paper this package accompanies: the factors, their limits, the shortcut formulas and the checks of the computation.

Wu Z (2026). osmoments: Exact Moments of Order Statistics. R package version 0.1.0. The engine that computes the moments of the normal order statistics.

Wu Z, Tong T (2026). osmoments: Exact means, variances and covariances of order statistics in R. Manuscript. The paper of the engine.

Wan X, Wang W, Liu J, Tong T (2014). Estimating the sample mean and standard deviation from the sample size, median, range and/or interquartile range. BMC Medical Research Methodology 14, 135.

Luo D, Wan X, Liu J, Tong T (2018). Optimally estimating the sample mean from the sample size, median, mid-range, and/or mid-quartile range. Statistical Methods in Medical Research 27(6), 1785-1805.

Shi J, Luo D, Weng H, Zeng XT, Lin L, Chu H, Tong T (2020). Optimally estimating the sample standard deviation from the five-number summary. Research Synthesis Methods 11(5), 641-654.

Balakrishnan N, Rychtar J, Taylor D, Walter SD (2022). Unified approach to optimal estimation of mean and standard deviation from sample summaries. Statistical Methods in Medical Research 31(11), 2087-2103.

McGrath S, Katzenschlager S, Zimmer AJ, Seitel A, Steele R, Benedetti A (2023). Standard error estimation in meta-analysis of studies reporting medians. Statistical Methods in Medical Research 32(2), 373-388.
